We need propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a tolyl (para?) ring with sulfonamide linking to another phenyl bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (para?).

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis: likely disconnections:

1) Amide formation: break C(=O)N bond between carbonyl carbon and aniline nitrogen. So precursor: α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2? Actually the acid part is phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which has the α,β-unsaturated amide substituent. So the amide carbonyl is attached to the same phenyl ring (c2). So the precursor after disconnection: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring via nitrogen: NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group and to the phenyl ring (c2). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the linking between two aromatic rings. So the amide is on the second phenyl ring (c2) attached to carbonyl.

Thus step 1: amide formation between cinnamic acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That yields the α,β-unsaturated amide.

Step 2: sulfonamide formation between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl phenyl? Actually we have NS(=O)(=O)c2... The sulfonyl group attached to phenyl (c2) and nitrogen attached to tolyl. So we can disconnect the S-N bond: precursor 1: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait the sulfonyl chloride would be ClSO2-c2ccc(... )? The sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl ring bearing the α,β-unsaturated amide substituent. So precursor: 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring (c2) which also has the α,β-unsaturated amide substituent. So we need that phenyl-sulfonyl chloride.

Thus step 2: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and that sulfonyl chloride.

Step 3: formation of the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (c2-CHO) and malonic acid. The aldehyde is on the phenyl ring (c2) at the position where the side chain attaches. So we need phenyl-CHO (c2) with the sulfonyl group already attached? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring, not the side chain. The side chain attaches at para position relative to sulfonyl? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O)N... The sulfonyl phenyl is same as the phenyl bearing the side chain. So the phenyl has both sulfonyl group (attached to N) and the side chain (C=C-CO-NH-aniline). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would have the sulfonyl group attached to the phenyl, and the side chain as aldehyde (instead of acid). So step 3: Doebner modification to convert aldehyde to α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) on that phenyl.

Thus overall 3 steps.

Now we need to find template IDs for each transformation. We can search for templates matching functional groups.

Step 1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid? Actually the acid is aromatic carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid). Use functional_groups_broken: aromatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide. Let's search.
